task.prompt: The orders dashboard query has become slow as the table grew; speed it up without changing the results.
task.proposed_action: add a composite B-tree index on the queried columns (customer_id, created_at) to the orders table

gold_label.rationale: The only document in the corpus is PEP 8 (`Status: Active`), the Style Guide for Python Code, which states its scope verbatim: "This document gives coding conventions for the Python code comprising the standard library in the main Python distribution." It even yields authority where it does apply: "Many projects have their own coding style guidelines. In the event of any conflicts, such project-specific guides take precedence for that project." Coding conventions say nothing about database schemas, query plans, or B-tree indexes, so no decision in the corpus governs the proposed action; the correct verdict is permitted with no governing decision, and the adherent behaviour is to proceed without inventing a prohibition. The trap is that PEP 8 is topically adjacent to any Python codebase, and an arm that retrieves it and over-applies it as a constraint on database indexing — or blocks the change pending naming/style concerns it does not actually impose here — commits the false_prohibit failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: the test is recognising that the retrieved neighbour governs a different subject matter, and deterministic retrieval that returns nothing binding should beat an LLM-mediated arm tempted to manufacture a rule. Gold label authored from the pinned PEP texts (python/peps@f866e77) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
